claim: Moving exact steps (arithmetic, long procedures) from the model's head into an interpreter or program raises accuracy, and the gain grows as the step gets harder for in-head work.
agent_test: Same model, same token budget: in-head arithmetic/enumeration vs code-executed on a numeric-scale ladder; score by exact match.

claim: A written scratchpad of intermediate steps lets models do multi-step computation they fail at in one pass (polynomial evaluation 8.8 to 20.1 few-shot, 31.8 to 50.7 fine-tuned). Nearly half of wrong written chains (46%) are slips that code could fix.
agent_test: Compare scratchpad-only vs scratchpad plus code check at equal tokens; count slips fixed.

claim: Interleaving reasoning with real actions and observations beats reasoning alone or acting alone (ALFWorld best trial 71% vs Act 45% vs BUTLER 37%; HotpotQA EM 33.8 vs CoT 28.9).
agent_test: Ablate observation feedback from the loop (model reasons without running anything) at equal tokens.

claim: Interface design alone moves agent success by several points with the model fixed: SWE-agent Lite 18.0 with lint-on-edit vs 15.0 without vs 10.3 no edit tool; summarised search 18.0 vs iterative 12.0; 100-line viewer 18.0 vs full file 12.7; shell-only 11.0 (7.33 without demo). Single run per cell, one model. Gap search: Agentless (program-owned pipeline, no model tool choice) scored 32.00% on SWE-bench Lite vs SWE-agent 18.33% (GPT-4o) and 23.00% (Claude 3.5 Sonnet); mini-swe-agent (bash only, about 100 lines) is reported above 74% on Verified. The 2024 interface gains are era-specific and no feature-by-feature ablation with variance exists from another group.
schema_part: Design view: program shows short filtered views
agent_test: Vary viewer size and feedback verbosity on our harness, 3 seeds, equal tokens.

claim: More environment information can hurt: full-file viewer, iterative search and full history scored lower than bounded or summarised views; CoThinker social overhead hurt instruction following (0.95 vs 1.03). Gap search: at equal thinking tokens one chain beat 5 multi-agent layouts from 1000 tokens up (mean accuracy 0.418 vs 0.379 sequential at 1000; 0.426 vs 0.387 at 10000).
agent_test: Bounded-view vs full-view of the same state in a single task family at equal tokens.

claim: Without outside feedback, self-revision does not help and often hurts (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 then 41.8; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0); oracle labels give the apparent gains (89.7). The signal must come from the environment.
agent_test: Self-critique round vs code/test-execution round at equal tokens on a checkable task.

claim: Environment-grounded verification is the most valuable part of an embodied loop: Voyager without self-verification loses 73% of items, random curriculum loses 93%.
agent_test: Remove the verification step from our loop only; keep tokens equal.

claim: Humans make zero errors on externally enforced rules; all errors were on internal rules, and difficulty fell as more rules moved outside (Zhang and Norman 1994, 18 subjects, errors p<.001 internal vs external). Effect is partly constraint enforcement, not only load.
agent_test: Rule stated in prompt vs rule enforced by a validator that rejects bad moves; compare violation rate.

claim: Epistemic actions exist: Tetris players rotate pieces physically (about 100-300 ms) rather than mentally (about 800-1200 ms) and verify position by moving to the wall more as drop height rises. Evidence is descriptive with 3 pilot subjects for the timing.
agent_test: Allow or forbid cheap probe actions (run, print, reformat) before the answer commit at equal tokens.

claim: People offload more when less confident, and offload more than is optimal (reminder bias); offloading still raised hit rate 88.1% vs 82.7% (N=363). Loss framing reduces over-offloading. For an agent the analogue is gating tool calls on a calibrated signal. Gap search: a prompted tool-need check is a weak gate (MetaTool decision accuracy 61.9% vs 50.0% for always-call, Llama3-8B).
agent_test: Tool call always vs only when confidence is below threshold, equal token budget; measure unneeded calls.

claim: The 'internet or phone presence harms memory/cognition' family is weak: Brain-drain meta-analysis pooled |g|=0.14 (22 studies, 43 effects, I2=61.8%), memory only significant; Google-effect meta-analysis has CI 0.12 to 2.13; Sparrow 2011 reportedly failed to replicate (not opened); handwriting advantage reportedly shrank (not opened). Gap search: Ward 2017 Experiment 2 preregistered replication N=383 found no effect (OSpan location F(2,377)=0.10, p=.91); Sparrow Experiment 1 failed in Camerer 2018 (N=104 then 234 pooled) and again in Hesselmann 2020 (N=89, BF01=5.07); Camerer overall 13 of 21 replicated at about half the original effect; a 2023 meta-analysis (k=56, n=7093) finds only working memory significant. Original Ward and Sparrow effect sizes were not read.
agent_test: Not needed; avoid claims that offloading degrades the model.

claim: Using an LLM as the external aid reduces memory of one's own output (15 of 18 LLM users could not quote their essay vs 2 of 18 for search and brain-only). Small preprint.
agent_test: None on the agent; implies keeping a program-readable log.

claim: Multi-agent or social setups do not reliably reduce load: MAST finds 14 failure modes in 1600+ traces; verification added +15.6 points in ChatDev; CoThinker helps hard tasks, hurts instruction following, and its shared memory helped some models and hurt others while role styles helped all three. Gap search: with compute matched, a single chain matches or beats split contexts and debate from 1000 thinking tokens up; debate beats CoT in about 15% of 36 configurations and rarely beats self-consistency; multi-agent helps when the single context is corrupted (heavy degradation) or the single-agent score is low (below about 45%), and hurts sequential planning by 39 to 70%.
schema_part: G4 (same-model agents are not independent checkers)
agent_test: Equal-compute: one chain vs split-contexts vs self-consistency on the same hard set.

claim: A harness that gives symbolic perception and state memory helps strong reasoning models on games (o3 Tetris 31 to 42, o1 13 to 35) but not weak ones (gpt-4o 14.7 to 14.0). Gap search: Kim 2026 finds coordination gains vanish above a single-agent score of about 45%; a bash-only 100-line agent is reported above 74% on SWE-bench Verified. Direct weak-model harness-on/off tests at equal tokens are still missing.
agent_test: Run harness on/off on a weaker and a stronger model, equal tokens.

claim: Giving the solution algorithm does not move the reasoning-model collapse on Tower of Hanoi (N=7-8), but the result is contested: an output-limit and format artefact explains much of it; asking for a generating function fixes Hanoi. Gap search: Lawsen reports models write the 15-disk solution as a Lua function in under 5,000 tokens but gives no counts; Shojaee et al. reply that first errors come at about 15% of an N=8 solution (move 40 of 255) and a temperature-zero run does not change the collapse. No measured pass rate for code-emitting models at 8 to 15 disks was found.
schema_part: Design view: program executes long procedures
agent_test: Model emits move list vs model emits program that the harness runs, N=8-12 disks.

claim: Letting the agent re-shape its workspace (Martin and Schwartz's key manipulation) has no LLM test, and the original paper was never opened by any of three agents; the manipulatives literature is only summarised at abstract level. Gap search: Martin and Schwartz abstract read (Experiments 4-5: adapting unstructured material transferred better than well-structured material); the full paper is still unread. The think tool (a fixed scratch tool) gave airline pass^1 0.404 alone vs 0.584 with an example prompt and retail 0.812 vs 0.783. No editable-vs-fixed LLM test exists.
agent_test: Fixed scratch template vs agent-editable scratch files, same tools, equal tokens.

claim: A persistent store of verified skills or failures written from real outcomes helps (Reflexion HumanEval 91 vs 80; ALFWorld +22; Voyager skill library prevents plateau) but gains depend on informative feedback such as unit tests. Gap search: vendor numbers only (memory tool plus context editing +39%, editing alone +29%, internal eval); Laban 2025 shows a fresh consolidated message removes the multi-turn loss of 39% while restating earlier turns recovers 15-20%.
agent_test: Memory of verified failures vs memory of unverified self-notes, equal tokens.

claim: Hutchins 1995 (ship navigation) and Latour's reading that tools change the task rather than amplify ability are qualitative and unmeasured; a claim that the calculator did not help in the power-loss episode is an unverified snippet. Gap search: book text could not be opened (401); still unverified.
agent_test: None; framing only.

claim: Concrete or situated material can look worse only because the situated condition was weak (Trninic et al. 2020 replication of Kaminski 2008 found better concrete examples matched or beat abstract); when testing environment help, the environment arm must be as well built as the control.
agent_test: Pre-check each environment arm in a pilot before the main run.

claim: Epistemic probes: models choose them badly and few-shot planner traces do not fix it (o3-mini, 5 trials per scenario; first-take accuracy 0 to 40% under hidden or distractor cases). A program-side information-gain rule (Uncertainty of Thoughts) reports a 38.1% average success gain over direct prompting, not at equal tokens.
agent_test: Probe chosen by the model vs probe chosen by an information-gain rule in the harness, equal total tokens, 3 seeds, score answer accuracy and tokens spent on probes.

claim: Sequential tasks and already-strong single agents should not get extra voices or splits: Kim 2026 (260 configurations) finds -39% to -70% on planning and negative returns once the single agent exceeds about 45%; Tran 2026 finds the single chain better from 1000 thinking tokens up, except when the context is heavily corrupted. Use as a gate.
agent_test: Gate: run the voice step only if single-pass score on a probe set is below 45% or context noise is high; compare to always-on at equal tokens.

claim: A model re-reading its own earlier prose is a measured failure source: multi-turn instructions cost 39% on average vs one message, models lean on their own early wrong answers, and restating helps only 15-20% of the loss. A consolidated fresh message removes the loss. No direct test of a program-held log vs prose at equal tokens exists.
schema_part: Design view: program holds state, rebuilds a fresh view
agent_test: Program-held verified-results table rendered each step vs full transcript, same model, equal tokens.

claim: A prompted check of whether a tool is needed is only a weak gate (MetaTool, Llama3-8B: 61.9% decision accuracy vs 50.0% for always calling; hidden-state gate 65.0%; 84.3% after fine-tuning). Simple tasks gain little from a scratch tool (think tool retail 0.812 vs 0.783).
schema_part: G1/G7 gate on tool and scratch steps
agent_test: Gate on a calibrated confidence or a cheap pre-check vs model self-report; count unneeded calls and accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Program-owned control flow can match or beat model-chosen tool use: Agentless (fixed localise-repair-validate) 32.00% at about $0.70 on SWE-bench Lite vs SWE-agent 18.33% to 23.00% at $1.62 in the same table. This does not show which SWE-agent feature matters.
schema_part: Design view: the program is the environment
agent_test: Fixed pipeline vs model-chosen tool loop on our tasks, same model, equal tokens.
